title: Chase the Series: Southeast Asia's Multi-City Race Tours
meta_description: The same race brand, run across multiple cities in the same season -- a genuinely common Southeast Asia format that lets runners collect an entire series rather than a single race.
dek: A handful of race brands in Southeast Asia don't run once a year in one city -- they tour, with the same format and branding repeated across several cities in the same season. These are the region's clearest examples.

sections.heading: The National MILO Marathon: A National Tour, City by City
paragraphs: The National MILO Marathon runs its full five-distance format -- 1km through 21.1km -- across multiple Philippine city legs, including Tagbilaran, Cebu, and Cagayan de Oro, giving runners in different parts of the country access to the same well-established race brand without traveling to a single national event.

For a runner chasing every leg, this format effectively turns one race brand into a mini race-trip series within a single country, with each city leg offering its own local flavor around the same core distance lineup.

sections.heading: Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia and PUMA Philippine Half Marathon Series
paragraphs: The Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia runs legs in Iloilo and Manila before culminating in a National Finals event, explicitly building toward a series conclusion rather than treating each leg as fully standalone. The PUMA Philippine Half Marathon Series runs its own separate legs in Clark and Cagayan de Oro, giving runners another genuinely multi-city option under one consistent race brand.

Both formats reward a runner who commits to more than one leg -- the "Trilogy" and "Series" framing in each name is doing real work, signaling that these are designed to be experienced as a set rather than picked individually.

sections.heading: HOKA Midnight Run Asia and Garmin Run: Series That Cross Country Lines
paragraphs: HOKA Midnight Run Asia runs its night-race format across Iloilo, Cebu, and Clark, while the Garmin Run Marathon Series extends its brand across both the Philippines and Malaysia -- genuine examples of a single race series operating across multiple cities and, in Garmin's case, multiple countries within the same regional footprint.

A brand-name series like this also tends to bring consistent race-day quality across its legs -- the same organizing standards, similar course marking and aid-station conventions -- which is a real advantage for a runner who wants predictability while still visiting a new city for each leg.

sections.heading: Why Chasing a Series Is a Different Kind of Race-Trip Goal
paragraphs: Committing to a full series rather than picking one race gives a race-trip plan a built-in structure across an entire season -- multiple destinations, one consistent brand and format to anchor the trip around, and often a series-completion medal or recognition as an added incentive for finishing every leg.

This is a genuinely different kind of goal from chasing the region's biggest single flagship events (covered in this site's Podium guide to the biggest race days) -- it rewards commitment and travel across a season rather than one big result on one specific day.

faqs.question: What are the biggest multi-city race series in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: The National MILO Marathon (Philippines, multiple city legs), Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia (Iloilo and Manila legs plus a National Finals), the PUMA Philippine Half Marathon Series (Clark and Cagayan de Oro legs), HOKA Midnight Run Asia (Iloilo, Cebu, and Clark), and the Garmin Run Marathon Series (spanning the Philippines and Malaysia) are among the clearest examples.

faqs.question: Is there a race series that crosses country lines in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the Garmin Run Marathon Series extends its brand across both the Philippines and Malaysia, running the same series format in multiple countries within the region rather than staying confined to one.

faqs.question: Why would I choose to chase a full race series instead of a single race?
faqs.answer: Committing to a full series gives a race-trip plan a built-in structure across an entire season -- multiple destinations under one consistent brand and format, often with a series-completion medal or recognition as an added incentive for finishing every leg.
